# Microsoft Azure Resource Graph management client library for .NET

The Microsoft Azure Resource Graph is an Azure service designed to extend Azure Resource Management by providing efficient and performant resource exploration with the ability to query at scale across a given set of subscriptions so that you can effectively govern your environment.

This library supports managing Microsoft Azure Resource Graph resources.

This library follows the [new Azure SDK guidelines](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/general_introduction.html), and provides many core capabilities:

    - Support MSAL.NET, Azure.Identity is out of box for supporting MSAL.NET.
    - Support [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/) for distributed tracing.
    - HTTP pipeline with custom policies.
    - Better error-handling.
    - Support uniform telemetry across all languages.

## Getting started 

### Install the package

Install the Microsoft Azure Resource Graph management library for .NET with [NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/):

```dotnetcli
dotnet add package Azure.ResourceManager.ResourceGraph
```

### Prerequisites

* You must have an [Microsoft Azure subscription](https://azure.microsoft.com/free/dotnet/).

### Authenticate the Client

To create an authenticated client and start interacting with Microsoft Azure resources, see the [quickstart guide here](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).

## Key concepts

Key concepts of the Microsoft Azure SDK for .NET can be found [here](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/dotnet_introduction.html).

## Documentation

Documentation is available to help you learn how to use this package:

- [Quickstart](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).
- [API References](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/?view=azure-dotnet).
- [Authentication](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/sdk/identity/Azure.Identity/README.md).

## Examples

Code samples for using the management library for .NET can be found in the following locations
- [.NET Management Library Code Samples](https://aka.ms/azuresdk-net-mgmt-samples)

## Troubleshooting

-   File an issue via [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/issues).
-   Check [previous questions](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/azure+.net) or ask new ones on Stack Overflow using Azure and .NET tags.

## Next steps

For more information about Microsoft Azure SDK, see [this website](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/).

## Contributing

guide][cg].

This project welcomes contributions and suggestions. Most contributions

proposals.subtype: Typed history operations over raw request/pipeline execution
proposals.explanation: GetResourcesHistory/GetResourcesHistoryAsync null-check the ResourcesHistoryRequest, start a diagnostic scope, create a RequestContext with the token and obtain a raw request using ResourcesHistoryRequest.ToRequestContent. They process it through the pipeline, wrap the deserialized dictionary with the raw response and reject a null dictionary using RequestFailedException. Failures mark the scope then rethrow; async execution uses ConfigureAwait(false). This is the plural ResourcesHistory API, not the disabled singular ResourceHistory API.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Both complete typed operation bodies are explicitly implemented in src/Custom/Extensions outside Generated rather than inferred from a generated method signature.

proposals.subtype: Raw response object values preserved as BinaryData
proposals.explanation: DeserializeResourcesHistory parses the BinaryData response with the configured JsonDocumentOptions, returns null for a top-level JSON null and otherwise enumerates the top-level object into Dictionary<string,BinaryData>. Each value uses BinaryData.FromString(property.Value.GetRawText()), preserving its raw JSON representation instead of materializing a fixed result model. This helper itself does not translate parse errors.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The concrete private response decoder is explicitly implemented in src/Custom/Extensions outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Compiler-error-obsolete mockable history methods throw directly
proposals.explanation: The singular GetResourceHistory/GetResourceHistoryAsync pair accepts ResourcesHistoryContent and declares Response<BinaryData>/Task<Response<BinaryData>>, but both bodies directly throw NotSupportedException. Both are editor-hidden and Obsolete with error:true. The async-named method is not an async implementation and performs no request; its package recommendation is just an observed attribute/message.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The explicit deprecation attributes and throwing method bodies are supplied in src/Custom/Extensions outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Retained static history extension signatures reject calls

Neither body forwards through a mockable resource or checks receiver/content for null, despite the synchronous method's XML exception description.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Both explicit static extension bodies and their attributes occur in src/Custom/Extensions outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Protected constructor supplies a null second argument
proposals.explanation: The abstract Facet partial explicitly exposes protected Facet(string expression) with the active initializer this(expression, null). Its body is empty, but the initializer adapts the construction signature. The other constructor implementation and claimed historical binary-compatibility baseline are not supplied.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: This concrete protected constructor initializer is in src/Custom/Models outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: History content constructor initializes change-tracking lists
proposals.explanation: The public ResourcesHistoryContent() constructor initializes both Subscriptions and ManagementGroups with separate ChangeTrackingList<string> instances. It does not initialize Query or Options or validate their content.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The nonempty collection-initializing constructor is implemented in src/Custom/Models outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Internal constructor stores supplied model and raw-data state
proposals.explanation: The five-argument internal ResourcesHistoryContent constructor assigns subscriptions, query, options, managementGroups and serializedAdditionalRawData directly to the model's state without copying or explicit validation. The same capture declares public get-only IList<string> collection properties and get/set Query/Options; get-only collection access does not make the lists immutable.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The explicit internal state-restoring constructor and public state declarations are supplied in src/Custom/Models outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Conditional model JSON writer with non-wire raw-data preservation
proposals.explanation: IUtf8JsonSerializable.Write delegates using WireOptions; IJsonModel.Write emits an object envelope around JsonModelWriteCore. The core normalizes W via GetFormatFromOptions, rejects non-J formats, conditionally writes subscription/management-group string arrays and defined query/options, and emits _serializedAdditionalRawData only outside W mode. Extra values use WriteRawValue on NET6_0_OR_GREATER or JsonDocument/JsonSerializer otherwise.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete explicit interface writers and property-by-property core are implemented in src/Custom/Models outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Mode-aware JSON reader captures unknown fields only outside wire mode
proposals.explanation: IJsonModel.Create normalizes format, rejects non-J input and parses the reader into the handwritten deserializer. That helper defaults options to WireOptions, returns null for JSON null, reads known query/options and string-list fields, skips null list/options values, and captures unknown properties as raw BinaryData only when options.Format is not W. Missing/null lists become ChangeTrackingList<string> instances before invoking the captured state constructor.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Both the explicit interface reader and complete property-dispatch deserializer are in src/Custom/Models outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: JSON-only BinaryData persistence adapter with explicit writer context
proposals.explanation: The explicit IPersistableModel Write normalizes W, accepts J and delegates to ModelReaderWriter.Write(this, options, AzureResourceManagerResourceGraphContext.Default); other formats throw. Create similarly accepts J, parses BinaryData with JsonDocumentOptions and calls the captured deserializer. GetFormatFromOptions returns "J". The explicit context argument is observed, not proof of AOT support or successful runtime serialization.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The concrete BinaryData read/write/format-selector implementations are supplied in src/Custom/Models outside Generated.

decisions.reason: Both complete methods at lines 41-68 and 90-117 are handwritten typed public operations in Custom that create a request via the RestClient request builder, execute it through the pipeline, and return a decoded typed response. The category and reusable typed-wrapper pattern are plausible for this operation wrapper; generator addressability is a possibility, not a claim that the captured request builder was itself generated.

Lines 119-134 explicitly decode a top-level JSON object into a dictionary of raw JSON BinaryData values, preserving each property's GetRawText; this is a separate response projection used by both typed operations. The helper does not catch JSON parsing failures. The catalog's raw-response-to-result projection describes this reusable shape, and a generator could plausibly emit the mapping.

The captured singular mockable methods are disabled throw-only API stubs, not convenience helpers wrapping generated operations. Their Obsolete(error: true) attributes prohibit ordinary new compilation, so the existing backward-compatibility-shim catalog definition (which says it keeps retired APIs compiling) overstates the observed behavior. The version-specific reason for retaining these signatures is not independently established.

decisions.reason: The protected single-string Facet constructor delegates to a two-argument constructor with null at lines 16-18, supplying an actual additional model constructor shape outside Generated. Its comments allege a compatibility history, but that baseline and the delegated constructor's implementation are not supplied; the proposal appropriately avoids asserting either as a proven fact.

The explicit public no-argument model constructor initializes two separate change-tracking lists at lines 47-51. This is observable collection initialization distinct from the serializer and matches the catalog's model-default-value description; it plausibly could be emitted by a generator.

The internal five-argument constructor only assigns deserialized state and raw-data storage at lines 59-66; the captured deserializer invokes it at line 158. It is an implementation detail of the reader assessed in the proposal keyed ee9e1c3a, not an independent alternative public model-construction behavior. Its separate model-alternate-constructors classification would double-count the same serialization behavior; public properties are considered separately as an omission.

Lines 14-80 implement a concrete property-by-property JSON writer in Custom, conditionally serialize known members and serialize unknown raw values only outside W mode. This is a distinct outgoing serialization behavior consistent with custom-model-json-serialization; the NET6 branch and fallback are both directly visible, without assuming execution or AOT support.

Lines 82-159 implement the independent incoming JSON path: dispatch known fields, leave skipped null collection/option values absent, capture unknown raw JSON outside W mode and substitute change-tracking lists for missing or null lists. It is property-by-property handwritten model deserialization, not merely a duplicate of the outgoing writer.

Lines 161-190 implement a separate BinaryData persistence interface and J-format routing over the JSON reader/writer, including a context-argument write and direct document parsing on create. The pattern names this reusable interface adapter, not a service, and the behavior could plausibly be generated. This finding concerns the additional persistence entry points rather than counting the property-wise codec again; no runtime or AOT guarantee follows.
